title: Column update file representation when deletion vectors are present
summary: With a dense representation for column update files already agreed, Anurag Mantripragada asked what a column file should contain at positions the base file has deleted. Option 1 (positional alignment) keeps the base file's row count and writes filler values such as NULLs at deleted positions, so stitching is a zero-copy column swap. Option 2 (applied deletes) stores only live rows plus a _pos column, which keeps Parquet statistics accurate but needs a scatter operation that PyArrow and arrow-rs do not readily offer. Replies leaned toward Option 1: measurements showed the storage overhead of NULL filler is small, and reviewers from the Rust, Go and Delta side reported Option 1 is simpler to implement. Open points raised were padding trailing deleted rows on write, which statistics writers must correct, row-group misalignment between base and column files, and how equality deletes interact with column files. The thread ends without a formal decision.

positions.stance: Laid out the two options and found that Option 2 needs a scatter primitive that is cheap in Spark's ColumnVector but missing or costly in PyArrow and arrow-rs.
Option 1 without _pos is more naturally compatible with future column families because stitching relies on implicit row alignment.
Storage overhead and stats accuracy should not decide the choice; leans toward always writing _pos, and notes positional alignment needs the base row count to pad trailing deleted rows.
Supports Option 1 based on a Delta proof of concept where positional alignment kept the read path simple, and says arrow-rs and arrow-go lack the kernels Option 2 needs.
Neither option is blocked in iceberg-rust; sketched an Option 1 reader and flagged that misaligned Parquet row groups force periodic buffer copies when stitching.
The spec should state which statistics (null_count, value_count) writers must adjust for filler values and should describe compaction mechanics.

Not supporting equality deletes with column updates is a major limitation; proposed either evaluating them on the old base column values or materializing them as position deletes when the column file is written.
Reading old column values for equality deletes is too complex and inefficient, and silently rewriting equality deletes into DVs should be left to users.

outcome.note: Replies leaned toward Option 1 (positional alignment), but no decision is stated in the thread and the question of equality-delete handling was still being debated in the last messages.

why_it_matters: The choice fixes how every implementation (Java, Python, Rust, Go, C++) must write and stitch V4 column update files.
